web_events.query: US economic data release this week CPI GDP jobs
web_events.answer: The upcoming US economic data releases this week include the July Consumer Price Index (CPI) on August 12, Federal Reserve decision, GDP, and PCE reports on July 29 and 30. The July jobs data will be pivotal in assessing the Federal Reserve's future interest rate outlook. The June CPI index stood at 3.5%, while the core CPI index was 2.6%. The June unemployment rate was 4.2%. The Federal Reserve left interest rates on hold, and the probability of two or more rate hikes this year increased to 54.

web_events.query: Federal Reserve speech this week monetary policy
web_events.answer: The Federal Reserve is expected to hold interest rates steady at 5.25%–5.50% this week, with markets focusing on the tone of the statement and Chair Powell’s comments for future rate move indications. Fed Chairman Kevin Warsh is unlikely to raise interest rates due to risks associated with prejudging task forces, temporary price shocks, and political dynamics. The Fed will release its policy decisions on Wednesday at 2 p.m. Eastern time, followed by a news conference at 2:30 p.m. Eastern time.

web_events.query: China PMI economic data this week
web_events.answer: China's official manufacturing Purchasing Managers' Index (PMI) fell to 49.2 in July from 50.3 in June, indicating a contraction in factory activity. The composite PMI also dropped to 49.3, the lowest since the pandemic ended in 2022. The sub-index for new orders and new export orders both contracted, signaling a slowdown in both domestic and international demand. The construction and services PMI also slumped to record lows, reflecting broader economic weakness.
